identity.description:
Add the D4c experiment tooling: replay, size groups, --models, --stage1 and --max-cost

## Summary

The tooling of the D4c experiments (TICKETS.md, D4c, "Shared parts" and E1 stage 1). Code and tests only. No experiment ran, and no test makes a model call or runs `codex`.

- **S2, `pr-review replay`.** It verifies the stored candidates of an eval again with the first verifier of one arm (`--verifier backend:model:effort`, `--prompt score|truth|bands`), and scores the result as the eval does. It makes no escalation, merge or cap call, and counts the results in the escalation band. `--arm stored` is the comparison arm. It needs no verifier call, and it also gives the escalation figures of E3 from the records. Other options: `--candidates` takes candidates from a reviewer outside the pipeline, `--severity finding|pr` is the severity step of E3b (no tools), `--sample` and `--seed` make the fixed-seed sample of E3, and `--resume` and `--max-cost` work as in the eval. The report gives the posted, truth, severity and by-score figures in total and for each case, so a bootstrap over the cases can use them. The `codex` backend exits 2 before any call until the Codex call takes a model and an effort; another session adds those options.
- **S3, `pr-review eval-sizes`.** It gives the changed lines of each case from `diff.patch`, and three groups of about equal count.
- **S4, `pr-review eval --models target=model:effort,...`.** It sets the model and effort of named reviewers, or of `all`, for one run.
- **E1 stage 1, `pr-review eval --stage1`.** It runs the reviewers with no verifier, stores the raw candidates (`stages.candidates`, with `identity.mode: "stage1"`), and matches them to the goldens with the raw judge. `eval-report --by-reviewer` gives the same per-reviewer figures from any eval directory, so S1 and a stage 1 arm compare on one rule.
- **`eval --max-cost` and `EXIT_STOPPED = 4`.** These set a dollar limit for each window.
- **The effort of each call** is now in `cost.queries[].effort`.
- The verifier decision of a first result is now one function, `decideFirst` in `src/verify/index.ts`. The run and the replay both call it. The behaviour of `verifyFinding` does not change.

## The `--max-cost` overshoot

- `eval --max-cost` counts the run queries and the judge queries of each repeat. It checks the limit before each repeat. A repeat that runs at the limit runs to its end, so the spend can pass the limit by at most one repeat. A repeat of the full pipeline costs about $4.75 on average ($133 / 28 cases). Plan for the most expensive case of the set, not for the mean.
- `replay --max-cost` counts every verifier, severity and judge call. It checks the limit before each call. The calls in flight run to their end, so the overshoot is at most the concurrency times the largest cap of one call: 5 × $0.50 = $2.50 by default, or 5 × $1 = $5 with `--severity pr`. A judge call caps at $0.25.

## Record audit (item 5 of the goal)

I checked this against `src/schemas/record.ts` and the 28 D8 records (tool version 0.12.0, read only). All 28 parse with the new schema.

| Item | Record field |
| --- | --- |
| The candidates of each pass before the verifier | `stages.reviewers[].findings`, with `.name` and `.pass`. The dropped findings are in `.dropped`, with the reason. |
| The candidates that went to the verifier, in dedupe order | A full run: `stages.verifications[]`, with `.finding` and `.sources`. A stage 1 run: `stages.candidates[]` (new). |
| Each verifier result | `stages.verifications[].first` |
| Each escalation and its result | `stages.verifications[].escalated`. The outcome is in `.final`, `.passed`, `.unsure` and `.rejected`. |
| The cost of each call | `cost.queries[].cost_usd` and `.duration_ms`. A verifier or escalation entry names `.verification`. A reviewer entry names `.reviewer` and `.pass`. |
| The model of each call | `cost.queries[].model` |
| The effort of each call | `cost.queries[].effort` (new). A record from before 0.15.0 has none, so take the effort from `identity.models` and `identity.selected_reviewers`. |
| The description of the verifier input | `identity.description` |
| The git facts of the verifier input | Not stored. `identity.history` says only whether the block was built and cut. The replay makes the facts again from the case clone with the gather code of the run. |

For E7 (passes and the dedupe key): the passes and spans of each reviewer finding are in `stages.reviewers`. `eval-report --by-pass` already reads them.

## Decisions taken on a recommendation (each one can be reversed before the merge)

- Replay posted figures compare only with other replays: there is no escalation, no merge and no cap. `--arm stored` is the comparison arm.
- The five bands map to the scores 5, 25, 50, 75 and 95 (`prompts/verifier-bands.md`), so the threshold and the escalation band work unchanged.
- `--stage1` turns the raw judge on always.
- The size groups use the default generated globs only. The command makes no clone, so it reads no repo config.
- The severity roles are eval roles. `finding` has 5 turns, $0.50 and 300 s. `pr` has 5 turns, $1 and 600 s.

## Known limits

- The golden match and the posted figures of a replay reuse `scoreRecord` through a minimal record view (`scoringView` in `src/eval/replay/index.ts`). This breaks if `scoreRecord` reads more of the record when extras are off.
- The E1 Sonnet arms need `--allow-same-judge`, because the judge is Sonnet 5.5.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` (1589 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`
- [x] `scripts/check-version-bump.sh` gives 0.14.0 to 0.15.0
- [x] Each new test file failed at its red commit (checked again by the lead at the red commits of the stage 1 and replay tests)
- [ ] No paid probe yet. It needs the principal's word.
